_rules: Edit only 'passes' (and 'notes'). Set passes=true only after `./init.sh check <id>` exits 0. Items run in order unless deps allow otherwise. Adding new items is fine; deleting or weakening a check is not.
_strategy: Static checks first (compile, fidelity, reachability, lint, structure), then smoke tests, then automatic behaviour checks: hidden, muted, scripted runs (tests/replays/) compared by screenshot and trace, against the original under Wine where it matters (user, 2026-10-10: no user playtests). Refactors: tools/check/regress.sh (RT_DET=1, pixel- and state-hash-exact against the old build). Crashes are fixed as whole defect classes in tools/ or runtime/, never per address.

items.desc: The game's own CRT math (atan2 0x873250, exp 0x874C90 -- both through the fxam-classifying transcendental dispatcher) matches host libm within 1e-12 over a sign/zero/quadrant grid, evaluated at WinMain (RT_SELFTEST_CRT, runtime/core/log.c). items.desc: Project structure rules (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): hand-written files <= 300 lines, runtime/ target-neutral, a README.md per source dir, every submodule commit of ours recorded in third_party/patches/
Formatters and linters clean: clang-format + clang-tidy (C/C++), ruff (Python), shfmt + shellcheck (sh), Prettier + ESLint (web JS)
Deterministic mode: two native runs of play_now_match.txt (RT_DET=1) are state-hash identical at every 300th frame up to frame 15000 (into a match).
Deterministic mode ignores host timing: random host delays at every guest thread hand-over (RT_DET_CHAOS) leave the state hashes unchanged.
Netplay 1v1 over the relay server (server/): two native instances, each driving its own virtual pad, Scotland v New Zealand from Team Select into the match; equal state hashes over 15000 frames.
A desync is detected: one flipped guest byte on one instance (RT_NET_FAULT) stops both with a DESYNC report.

Drop-in in real browser pages, as players use it: the game boots straight in, the host's code comes from its Online panel, a friend opens their own game and types the code into the Join box 20 s later, catches up, gets the "You're in" toast, its keys reach its controller, hashes stay equal, and the host plays on after the friend leaves.

The web build's split giant functions behave like the originals: a native build with build/web-gen opens MY RUGBY and Squad Management without a fault (the split jump tables sent computed jumps to the wrong exit; MY RUGBY crashed in the browser).
